about.title: Irwindale Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Irwindale is a small city of about 1,437 residents, yet it carries a heavy share of traffic through Los Angeles County. The I-605 San Gabriel River Freeway, the I-210 Foothill Freeway, and Arrow Highway run through or beside town, and public records for 2025 list 162 injury collisions, 229 people hurt, and 2 traffic deaths. Behind each of those two deaths is a family working through grief while also facing paperwork, bills, and questions no one prepared them for. A wrongful death claim in California is a civil action, separate from any criminal case that may follow a fatal crash or workplace incident. It lets a spouse, domestic partner, children, and in some situations dependents or heirs seek compensation for funeral and burial costs, lost financial support, and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance. The deadline is two years from the date of death, and shorter if a public entity is involved. LawProactive is not a law firm. We connect Irwindale families with an independent attorney who reviews the situation for free and works on contingency.

items.question: My family member died in a crash on I-605 near Irwindale. Does the criminal case affect our claim?
items.answer: A wrongful death claim is a civil action and runs on its own track, separate from any criminal charges the district attorney may or may not pursue. You can bring a civil claim even if no one is charged, and the outcome of a criminal case does not decide your civil case. If road design or a government vehicle played a role, the deadline to give notice to a public entity is much shorter than two years, so it helps to speak with an attorney early.

items.question: Who is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: A surviving spouse or registered domestic partner and the children of the person who died have the first right to file. If there are none, certain dependents and heirs under California's intestate succession rules may be able to bring the claim. An attorney can confirm where your family falls and whether multiple relatives should join a single action.
